_instructions: All world entries live in a single World.json file under a 'world' array. Every entry requires name, tag, and type. All other fields are type-dependent.

world.name: Location name
world.tag: One-line summary: what it is and why it matters to the story
world.subtype: City | District | Casino | Brothel | Private_Club | Yacht | Capital City | Distant Kingdom | etc.
world.physical_description: Layout, materials, who uses it, its function in the story
world.sensory_description: Dominant sensory impression: smell, sound, light quality, texture
world._optional_location: also_known_as, owner, social_rules, prevents, forces, enables

world.name: Organization name
world.tag: One-line summary: what it is and why it matters
world.description: What it is, what it does, who runs it, what it wants
world._optional_org: prevents, forces, enables — each a single present-tense sentence about scene-level consequences

world.name: System name
world._note: Fields vary by subtype. Use the fields that apply: physical_description, sensory_description, social_rules, members, rules, slice_of_life_texture, currency, key_industries, trade_system, traditions, language_dialects, arts_entertainment

world.name: Event name
world.tag: One-line summary: when it happened and why it matters
world.when: When this happened relative to the story
world.implications: What this means for the characters going forward
